definition: Fecund means fertile, producing new life or ideas in teeming abundance.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word fecund. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know fecund should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The volcanic terraces are so fecund that farmers there joke about harvesting anything they happen to drop.
Productive stops short of fecund — a productive plot meets its quota and not much more.
Fruitful stops short of fecund — a fruitful season gives a good yield, while a fecund one buries you in zucchini and volunteer seedlings.

Prolific counts the output: a prolific author, a prolific vine — many works, many grapes, one after another. Fecund points at the generative power behind the output, the teeming fertility that keeps producing whether anyone asks or not. A prolific writer publishes constantly; a fecund imagination breeds more ideas than could ever be written down.

Bountiful praises what is given — a bountiful harvest, a bountiful host — generosity in the yield itself. Fecund looks earlier in the process, at the power to keep producing: soil, species, or minds teeming with new life. A bountiful table is loaded once; a fecund garden keeps loading it.
produces nothing at all

Fecund arrived whole from Latin fecundus, 'fruitful.' Its ancient root — meaning 'to nourish, to suckle' — does survive, but only in remote technical words like fetus, which no longer look or feel related. With no everyday cousin to give it away, fecund must be learned on its own.
Fecund means fertile, producing new life or ideas in teeming abundance.
Grandfather's back plot shamed the whole allotment: the same seed packets everyone bought produced double there, and neighbors swore his fecund half-acre could sprout a fence post if he watered it.
Fecund reaches past 'productive' — a productive plot earns its keep, but a fecund one seems to overflow with life on its own, generating more than anyone asked of it.
The word covers minds, too: a fecund mind breeds ideas the way rich soil breeds seedlings.
Fecund is the writer's and biologist's word; in everyday speech, fertile does the job.
Choose fecund when you want abundance with a hint of wonder or excess — fecund soil, a fecund imagination — production that outruns anyone's plans.
